title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
sourceTitle: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
synopsis: A work-farm transfer, a card table, a fishing trip, and a quiet Indian by a window who has been listening the whole time.

nodes.text: A nurse in starched white at a glass window with a clipboard. The road still runs toward Med Cart. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Smile big” and choosing “Stay quiet.” By Med Cart, the decision will already have changed who trusts you.

choices.consequence: You commit to smile big. By Med Cart, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You stay quiet. The decision moves you toward Med Cart and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: A small paper cup with three pills and a name on the side. Cards comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Refuse” and “Swallow.” In Med Cart, waiting would only let someone else define what your silence meant.

choices.consequence: You refuse. The decision moves you toward Cards and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You swallow. The decision moves you toward Cards and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Chief lifts the pillow with both hands. Choose “Look him in the eye” and Through the Window comes into view; choose “Close your eyes” and the road bends toward The Card Table. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Chief's Voice in play.

choices.consequence: You choose to look him in the eye. It opens the route to Through the Window, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You commit to close your eyes. By The Card Table, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You take the third path. The decision moves you toward Chief's Voice and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Chief lifts the sink and walks out into a morning that smells of cut grass. Somewhere, you are running with him. Somewhere else, you are at rest. The road into Through the Window began with “Look him in the eye” in Pillow; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

The men learn poker. They learn it well. They lose a thousand games to each other and not one to the house, ever again. The road into The Card Table began with “Close your eyes” in Pillow; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

He goes back to Canada through fields nobody owns. He talks now. Mostly to a stranger he keeps in his head, in a leather jacket, smiling like a mouth full of cards. The road into Chief's Voice began with “Take the third path” in Pillow; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
